blocks.text: The branch of chemistry that deals with the interconversion of electrical and chemical energy, electrical energy into chemical energy and chemical energy into electrical energy, is called electrochemistry.

blocks.title: Oxidation and reduction
blocks.text: Oxidation is a process involving the loss of one or more electrons; reduction is a process involving the gain of one or more electrons.

Fe2+ giving Fe3+ + e- and Zn giving Zn2+ + 2e- are oxidations: Fe2+ and Zn have lost electrons. Cl2 + 2e- giving 2Cl- and Cu2+ + 2e- giving Cu are reductions: Cl and Cu2+ have gained electrons. Oxidation and reduction always take place together, and the reactions in which this happens are called redox reactions. Photosynthesis, which provides food for the entire planet, and respiration, which keeps you alive, are both redox reactions. There are two ways of finding out whether a substance has been oxidised or reduced during a reaction: electron transfer, and changes in oxidation number.

blocks.caption: Redox basics: electron transfer, oxidation number rules and examples, disproportionation, and oxidising and reducing agents (original diagram after topics 10.1 to 10.5).
blocks.long_description: Losing electrons is oxidation, as when iron(II) becomes iron(III) or zinc becomes zinc ions; gaining electrons is reduction, as when chlorine becomes chloride or copper ions become copper. The oxidation number rules let these changes be tracked without writing electrons: elements are zero, fixed values are assigned to common atoms, and the numbers sum to the charge, which gives sulfur +4 in SO2, +6 in sulfate and manganese +7 in permanganate. When one element is both raised and lowered, as oxygen in decomposing hydrogen peroxide or chlorine in hot alkali, the reaction is a disproportionation. The substance that gains the electrons is the oxidising agent and the one that loses them the reducing agent, and matching the electrons lost and gained balances the dichromate-hydrochloric acid equation.

blocks.prompt: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electron transfer, with examples (Quick Check 10.1a).
blocks.explanation: Oxidation is loss of electrons: Zn gives Zn2+ + 2e-, Fe2+ gives Fe3+ + e-. Reduction is gain of electrons: Cu2+ + 2e- gives Cu, Cl2 + 2e- gives 2Cl-. The electrons lost by one species are gained by another, so the two always occur together in a redox reaction.

items: Electrochemistry: interconversion of electrical and chemical energy.
Oxidation = loss of electrons (Fe2+ to Fe3+, Zn to Zn2+); reduction = gain (Cl2 to Cl-, Cu2+ to Cu); always together in a redox reaction; traced by electron transfer or by oxidation number change.
